title: Quantum-Geometric Meissner Effect in Magnetized Color Superconductors
abstract: We find a quantum-geometric Meissner response in magnetized two-flavor color-superconducting (2SC) quark matter. Landau quantization quenches the transverse quasiparticle dispersion, suppressing the conventional Fermi-surface contribution and giving rise to a Meissner response governed by the quantum geometry of the Landau levels. In the strong-field regime, the response becomes dominated by the quantum metric of the lowest Landau level (LLL), and the leading scaling of the transverse Meissner mass is consequently set by the pairing gap, in contrast to the chemical potential scaling of conventional color superconductors. This unconventional scaling has a topological origin, as the LLL quantum metric is constrained by its Chern number. The reduced transverse Meissner mass provides potential implications for kHz quasi-periodic oscillations in magnetars.
summary: This work derives the Meissner effect in magnetized 2SC quark matter, showing that the response is governed by the quantum geometry of the lowest Landau level. The resulting transverse Meissner mass scales with the pairing gap, a topological feature, which suggests a potential signature for quasi-periodic oscillations observed in magnetars.
main_problem: To investigate the Meissner response in magnetized two-flavor color-superconducting (2SC) quark matter, focusing on the role of quantum geometry in the superconducting response.
main_result: The transverse Meissner mass scales with the pairing gap ($\propto |\Delta|$) rather than the chemical potential ($\propto \mu$), a result attributed to the topological constraints imposed by the Lowest Landau Level (LLL) quantum metric.
method: The Meissner mass is calculated from the static quadratic response of the thermodynamic potential using a spectral representation that explicitly incorporates Landau-level eigenstates and quantum geometric tensors.
model_or_system: The system is magnetized 2SC quark matter, analyzed using the Nambu–Gor’kov (NG) spinor and propagator. The analysis is performed in the strong-field and Isolated Landau-Level (ILL) limits.
key_observables: Transverse Meissner mass ($M^2$), quantum metric ($g_N$), and Chern number ($C$).
important_parameters: Pairing gap ($\Delta$), chemical potential ($\mu$), magnetic field strength ($	ilde{B}$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ILL limit ($|d_{NN'}| \gg |\Delta|$), and the strong-field regime ($\omega 	ilde{B} \gg \mu$) is crucial for the topological scaling.

paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the Meissner response by decomposing the NG propagator, calculating the polarization tensor, and isolating the quantum-geometric contribution in the ILL limit, leading to the final scaling laws.
why_interesting: The topological origin of the Meissner mass scaling provides a novel, field-theory approach to understanding superconducting responses in extreme astrophysical environments, linking condensed matter theory to high-energy astrophysics.
